Veradermics has announced positive results from the Phase III trial of the VDPHL01 tablet for baldness.

Veradermics reported that the prolonged-release minoxidil tablet VDPHL01 met all primary and secondary endpoints in the Phase III study. The trial involved 536 men with mild to moderate androgenetic alopecia.
According to the company's data, differences from placebo in hair counts, patient assessments, and investigator evaluations were seen as early as two months. By six months, non-vellus hair growth per square centimeter was 28.6 with once-daily dosing and 36.4 with twice-daily dosing compared to 6.6 with placebo. The developers stated that no serious adverse events related to the drug or cardiac events were reported.

The company plans to submit an application for approval to the FDA. If approved, this would be the first non-hormonal oral treatment for androgenetic alopecia.

📌 Watch-Only Wallets: Tracking Crypto Without Access to Funds

Main Points
⏺ A watch-only wallet lets users monitor balances and transactions without holding private keys
⏺ This setup is useful for large portfolios, cold storage, and address analysis
⏺ This post explains why monitoring assets doesn't require spending access

1️⃣ Core Idea — the app receives a public wallet address and displays its assets and transaction history.
2️⃣ Why It Helps — users can monitor long-term holdings without connecting the device that stores their private keys.
3️⃣ Use Cases — cold wallets, corporate treasuries, whale monitoring, and crypto portfolio accounting.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — the app cannot sign transactions without a key, but it may collect information about your addresses and financial activity.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — add only public addresses, verify supported networks, and never enter a seed phrase just to view balances.


Final Thoughts

You don't need to give an app control over your crypto just to monitor it. Separating viewing from signing reduces situations where private keys are exposed to unnecessary risk.

Democrats are turning Trump’s expanding personal wealth into a major weapon ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, arguing that while the president and his allies continue to accumulate fortunes, millions of Americans are struggling with rising prices and mounting household expenses.

The strategy is built around a message that appears to be gaining traction with voters: Washington politicians are getting richer while ordinary families are falling further behind. For Democrats, the issue is no longer simply about political ethics. It is about the direct impact of alleged corruption on the financial well-being of Americans.

Party strategists say polling has revealed an important shift in public sentiment. Voters are increasingly inclined to blame political corruption rather than corporate greed for their economic difficulties. That finding has helped Democrats make government accountability a central theme of their campaign to regain control of Congress.

The timing is significant. Persistent inflation has eroded purchasing power, while the cost of groceries, gasoline, housing and other essentials continues to weigh on household budgets. 

Wage growth has struggled to keep pace, leaving many Americans frustrated despite broader signs of economic activity. Democrats argue that the contrast with Trump's financial fortunes is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore. 

His family has expanded its cryptocurrency interests during his presidency, while financial disclosures indicate that Trump generated more than $1.4 billion from cryptocurrency ventures in 2025.

The controversy has also been fueled by questions surrounding the administration's handling of records related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. 

Trump's earlier promises to challenge Washington's powerful interests helped build his political image, but critics say recent developments have raised doubts about that commitment. Democratic campaigns are bringing the message directly to voters. In competitive congressional races, advertisements highlight lawmakers' stock trading, financial relationships with powerful industries and alleged benefits received through political connections. 

One campaign slogan captures the strategy: “Their Corruption Is Costing Us.” The White House rejects the accusations, insisting that Trump is fighting fraud, waste and abuse across the federal government. 

Administration officials argue that Democrats are ignoring efforts to protect taxpayers and are using corruption allegations for political gain. Republicans are also attempting to turn the issue against Democrats, pointing to disagreements over legislation restricting congressional stock trading. 

However, the growing debate over politicians' financial interests is creating challenges for both parties.Recent polling suggests that concerns about corruption extend beyond traditional party lines. Even among Republican-leaning voters, the share who believe Trump is using the presidency to enrich himself has increased. 

Democrats currently hold an advantage on the issue in several national surveys.Still, the political impact remains uncertain. Trump's most loyal supporters continue to dismiss allegations against him, arguing that his business background explains his wealth and questioning the financial conduct of Democratic politicians.

For Democrats, the challenge is to convince voters that corruption is not just another Washington scandal, but something that affects the price of everyday life. 

With the midterm elections approaching, they are betting that Americans who feel financially squeezed will pay attention to who is benefiting from political power — and who is paying the bill.

⚠️ Tether leads $15M funding for Mural to power AI agent payments 

👀 Tether has led a $15 million Series A funding round for New York-based Mural, supporting the financial technology company’s development of payment infrastructure for businesses and artificial intelligence agents. Mural plans to use the investment to expand internationally and develop the banking, payment and compliance services needed for software agents to conduct financial transactions.

🔔 Founded in 2022 by former Palantir engineers Sinclair Toffa and Chris Fernandes, the company provides infrastructure that businesses use to manage accounts, payment instructions, identity verification and regulatory requirements across banking networks and blockchains. Its customers include global payroll provider Deel, browser developer Opera and financial technology platform Axexo. Through Mural’s system, businesses can offer accounts holding dollars, local currencies and stablecoins without managing separate financial infrastructure for each payment method.

📌 The company reported processing $2.1 billion in payments for users across 128 countries since introducing its application programming interface in 2025. Payment volume recorded so far in 2026 is nearly six times its total for 2025. Mural has not disclosed the valuation attached to the latest funding round. Fortune reported that the company previously raised $5 million in seed financing in 2022, followed by additional capital from existing backers.
